title: Retool route selector to minimize lock contention and improve regional failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: The current route selector implementation uses a coarse-grained global lock and mutates shared routing state on the hot request path. Under regional spikes this causes lock contention, p99 latency amplification, and contributes to throttling/fallback churn. This ticket retools the selector: introduce a lock-free read path using snapshotting / sequence-numbered state, shard regional decision state to reduce cross-region coordination, and simplify the fallback decision tree to remove expensive synchronous probes. Goal is to reduce tail latency, lower CPU on routing hosts, and make regional failover more predictable.
acceptance_criteria: P99 generation+routing latency improvement >= 18ms on synthetic mixed-size text workloads compared to baseline
No correctness regressions: route decision A/B for existing unit tests must match previous behavior except in documented fallback ordering changes
End-to-end canary rollout in prod uses feature-flag and automatic rollback on error rate > 0.5% over baseline
New unit and integration tests covering concurrent updates and snapshot reads included
Deployment/upgrade plan documented with rollback steps and data migration notes
notes: Spike findings (02/2026): global-lock dominated >45% of scheduler CPU on routing-hosts during small-request 95th-percentile load
Trade-offs considered: RCU-style snapshots vs. per-request copy-on-write. Chosen: immutable snapshots + optimistic CAS updates for lower GC pressure in Go runtime
We will keep a thin compatibility shim that emits legacy fallback traces for 2 weeks after rollout to make rollback comparisons easier
This change touches routing hotpath - plan coordinated deploy with traffic splits, 10% -> 30% -> 70% -> 100% over 3 days
implementation_notes: Introduce RouteState v2 with sequence_number and immutability guarantees
Read path: atomic pointer swap to latest snapshot; readers never grab mutexes
Write path: builders create modified copies and CAS the global pointer; writers take short mutex only during build
Regional shards: split policy tables by geo_shard_id to avoid cross-region lock storms
Fallback simplification: remove active probing on fast path; replace with async health-update stream used by selector
Compatibility: map old fallback priority field to new ordinal with conversion table in migration code
